Department.placement: Standalone. A list of departments away from any owner is the school's own structure screen; nothing owns a department.
Department.crossEntity: None. A department is written on its own; its head is a reference to Staff, not a write into it.
Department.openQuestions: Whether a department may have a second, acting head during a long absence. Modelled as one `staff_id` — a second head would be a link entity, and no research line asked for one.

Room.placement: Standalone reference data. Rooms are listed, filtered and reported on in their own right.
Room.crossEntity: None. A room's capacity seeds a section's capacity at timetabling, and that copy is deliberate: a room re-measured next year must not change a section already recruited to.
Room.openQuestions: Whether room bookings outside teaching (parents' evenings, examinations) belong here. Out of scope per research §8.

AcademicTerm.placement: Standalone. Almost every screen in the application is filtered by term, so it is a first-class list.
AcademicTerm.crossEntity: Closing a term is expected to close its sections and finalise its invoices. Neither is automated: both are decisions with money attached, and the closing checklist is the finance officer's `finance-drafts-past-census` report rather than a saga nobody watched run.
AcademicTerm.openQuestions: The academic year is a label here (`academic_year`), not a table — research §9.10. If year-level reporting ever needs its own record (year-group promotion, year-book), that is a roster change, not a field change.

Staff.placement: Standalone, and the model's person entity: every `_by_id` column in the document resolves here because no `User` entity is declared.
Staff.crossEntity: A member of staff going `on_leave` or `left` leaves their sections pointing at them; the `principal-teaching-cover-gap` report is what surfaces it. Deliberately not automated — reassigning a group mid-term is a timetabling decision, not a side effect of an HR field.
Staff.openQuestions: Whether a person may be both staff and guardian (a teacher whose child attends). Two records today, linked by nothing. Merging them would need a party model and was ruled out at Gate B.

Course.placement: Standalone. The curriculum list is a screen the whole school uses.
Course.crossEntity: None. Retiring a course does not touch its sections: past teaching and past results must survive it.
Course.openQuestions: Whether entry requirements for advanced courses should be modelled (a prerequisite link between courses) or left to the registrar. Left out at Gate B as scope.

Guardian.placement: Standalone. Two students sharing a guardian share this record — which is the whole reason a guardian is not a set of columns on the student.
Guardian.crossEntity: The primary-contact flag on `StudentGuardian` decides who an invoice reaches. Nothing writes it automatically; `finance-issued-without-payment` reads it.
Guardian.openQuestions: Whether a guardian who is also the billing party for a second family's child needs separating from the correspondence address. One address today.

Student.placement: Standalone, and the central artefact of the model.
Student.crossEntity: Suspension is written **onto** the student by the `SuspensionEscalation` saga when a conduct record records a suspension sanction — trigger `DisciplineIncident` → target `Student` → transition `enrolled|on_leave → suspended`. Withdrawal deliberately does *not* cascade: the term's invoice stands, which is the school's policy and the reason `Enrollment.withdrawn_on` is evidence rather than a trigger.
Student.openQuestions: Whether year-group rollover should be a workflow (advance every enrolled student by one year each August) or an administrative task. Left manual: a rollover that runs on the wrong date is expensive to unpick.

StudentGuardian.placement: Child of `Student` (§3.3.1: Q1 no — a list of links away from the child is not a screen; Q2 and Q3 yes). It appears as a tab on the student record, which is where the office looks for it.
StudentGuardian.crossEntity: None written automatically. The rule that exactly one guardian per student carries `is_primary_contact` is not enforceable by a rule that can only read the record being written — a second primary contact is a two-row fact — so it is a report, and named as such rather than promised as a refusal.
StudentGuardian.openQuestions: Whether `may_collect` needs an expiry (a court order with an end date). Boolean today.

AdmissionApplication.placement: Standalone. The admissions queue is the admissions officer's entire working screen.
AdmissionApplication.crossEntity: Acceptance creates a student and raises that student's first invoice — trigger `AdmissionApplication` → targets `Student` and `FeeInvoice` → create — through the `AdmissionToEnrolment` saga, gated by the `enrolOnAcceptance` action so it fires on acceptance and on nothing else.
AdmissionApplication.openQuestions: Whether an offer should expire automatically after its deadline. Not modelled: an expiry that runs unattended has told a family no, and the school wants a person to do that. `admissions-offers-unanswered` is the report that makes it a decision.

ClassSection.placement: Standalone. The timetable is a list of sections and it is opened daily.
ClassSection.crossEntity: Cancelling a section withdraws every enrolment on it — trigger `ClassSection` → target `Enrollment` → transition `pending|enrolled → withdrawn` — through `SectionCancellation`. The enrolment counter is maintained by the `Enrollment` hooks rather than by this entity, and `registrar-counter-disagrees` is the report that notices when a hook fails silently.
ClassSection.openQuestions: One day and one period per section keeps the timetable readable; a subject needing two slots a week is modelled as two sections of the same course. Confirmed as a deliberate simplification, and the one most likely to need revisiting in a real school.

ClassSession.placement: Standalone — argued at Gate B and recorded there. *Today's sessions across every section* is the register screen, which is the most-opened list in the application; a session is identified by its own date and time, not by its position in a section.
ClassSession.crossEntity: Closing a register updates each enrolment's attendance rate — that is written by the `AttendanceRecord` hooks, one mark at a time, rather than by the session.
ClassSession.openQuestions: Whether a cancelled session should generate excused marks for the group, so the statutory return has a row per student. Not modelled: `register_taken` staying false on a cancelled session is the honest record, and `teacher-registers-not-taken` excludes cancelled sessions for exactly that reason.

Enrollment.placement: Standalone. The registrar's working list is enrolments across sections, not a tab on one section.
Enrollment.crossEntity: Creating an enrolment increments the section's counter (`incrementSectionEnrolment`); changing its status maintains it (`maintainSectionEnrolment`). Capacity is checked in the `checkSectionCapacity` handler and **not** as a rule — §10.4's second route: the condition names a fact about the section, which a `when:` cannot read, so a rule written that way would have been seeded, drawn by the viewers, and inert.
Enrollment.openQuestions: Whether a clash (two enrolments in the same day and period) should be refused as well as reported. Same limitation as capacity: it is a two-row fact. A handler could refuse it; today it is `registrar-timetable-clashes`.

AttendanceRecord.placement: Child of `ClassSession` — the register is a tab on the session, and a mark away from its session means nothing.
AttendanceRecord.crossEntity: Each mark updates the enrolment's `attendance_rate` (`updateEnrolmentAttendanceRate` on create, `correctEnrolmentAttendanceRate` on a correction), which is the number the pastoral team sorts by and the statutory floor is measured against.
AttendanceRecord.lifecycle: None, deliberately. `present`, `late`, `absent` and `excused` are classifications rather than stages: a mark is corrected, not advanced, and drawing a machine over them would refuse a correction with a 403. `is_authorised` is kept separate from the mark for the same reason — an absence can be re-authorised later without rewriting the register.
AttendanceRecord.openQuestions: Whether a correction should keep the original mark for audit. Today it is an update; the statutory obligation is satisfied by the `updated_at` and audit trail the generated application writes.

Assessment.placement: Standalone. A teacher's "what have I got to mark" spans every section they teach.
Assessment.crossEntity: Publishing an assessment is expected to create one result row per enrolled student. Not modelled as a saga: a `CreateEntity` step writes one row, and the fan-out over a group belongs in the application. Stated here rather than left as an assumption.
Assessment.openQuestions: Whether weights should be refused when they would take a section past 100. Two-row fact again, so `hod-weights-not-adding-up` is the report.

AssessmentResult.crossEntity: None outward. Inward: `copyAssessmentMaximum` stamps `max_score` from the paper at creation — the §10.4 first route, a column that earns its place, and the reason `refuseScoreAboveMaximum` can be a rule at all.
AssessmentResult.openQuestions: Whether a re-grade should be a second record rather than an edit. An edit today, with `marked_by_id` carrying the moderator.

FeeInvoice.placement: Standalone. The finance office works a list of invoices.
FeeInvoice.crossEntity: Its totals are written by the `FeeInvoiceLine` and `Payment` hooks, never keyed; its status is moved by the two payment sagas. `mark_overdue` is a scheduled move rather than a rule — a rule cannot read the clock — and it is called out here so nobody expects the transition to fire itself.
FeeInvoice.openQuestions: Instalment plans. A plan is a schedule of expected payments, which this model does not carry; today a plan is an understanding between the office and a family, and `finance-debt-ageing` is what shows whether it is being kept.

FeeInvoiceLine.placement: Child of `FeeInvoice`. The noun is the tell.
FeeInvoiceLine.crossEntity: Every write recalculates the invoice's total — `addLineToInvoiceTotal`, `recalculateInvoiceTotal` and `removeLineFromInvoiceTotal`, one per event, because a handler name is a function name in the generated per-entity module and the compiler keeps only the first binding of a name that serves two events. `priceLine` computes `line_total` from quantity and unit amount at creation, so a rounding decision is made once and shown identically on every statement afterwards.
FeeInvoiceLine.openQuestions: Tax. The school's fees are not taxed in the modelled jurisdiction, so no tax column exists — a school where they are would need one per line rather than one per invoice.

Payment.placement: Standalone. The daily takings list is payments across invoices.
Payment.crossEntity: `resolveInvoiceBalance` stamps `balance_before` before the write, `applyPaymentToInvoice` applies the money after it, and the rule then moves the invoice through `InvoiceSettlement` or `PartPaymentPosting`. That order is the §10.4 pattern stated exactly: a handler resolves, the rule decides and acts.
Payment.openQuestions: Instalment plans, and what a refund does to the invoice. A negative payment is still refused by `refuseNonPositivePayment`; money going back is a `Refund` against the payment, which never edits or deletes it. Nothing moves the invoice when a refund is paid — no saga reads `Refund` — so an invoice stays `paid` after its money has been returned, and `finance-refunds-awaiting-decision` is the queue a person works from.

DisciplineIncident.placement: Standalone. The pastoral team works a list of incidents.
DisciplineIncident.crossEntity: A suspension sanction suspends the student — trigger `DisciplineIncident` → target `Student` → transition `enrolled|on_leave → suspended` — through `SuspensionEscalation`. Nothing lifts the suspension automatically: `reinstate` is a person's decision, and `counsellor-current-suspensions` is the list it is made from.
DisciplineIncident.openQuestions: Read access is `counsellor` and `principal` only, so a teacher cannot record an incident — they report it to the pastoral team, who record it with the teacher named in `reported_by_id`. The alternative (teachers create and read every incident) was rejected against research §7's safeguarding line. Row-level scoping — a teacher seeing only incidents they reported — is an application concern that `%%rbac` cannot express, and it is the change to make if the school wants teachers to record directly. Welfare and child-protection concerns are not recorded here: `SafeguardingConcern` is a separate entity, on purpose, because a student may be at risk rather than at fault — and, unlike here, a teacher may create one.

ConsentRecord.placement: Standalone. The renewal queue — every consent that lapses in the next thirty days, across all students — is a list someone opens in its own right (`registrar-consents-expiring`), and a consent has its own identity: this guardian's decision about this student's participation, on a date.
ConsentRecord.crossEntity: None. Withdrawing a consent records when authority ended and does not stop anything by itself; no hook or saga reads `ConsentRecord`, so whoever acts on a trip, a photograph or a data share checks the record.
ConsentRecord.openQuestions: `expire` is a transition nobody triggers: like an invoice going overdue it is the clock's, so `registrar-consents-expiring` is the list a person acts from rather than a rule that fires. A guardian can read and withdraw consents through the `guardian` role, but `%%rbac` cannot scope that role to their own child — the same limitation `02-cross-cutting.md` records for every guardian-readable entity.

SupportPlan.placement: Standalone. The counsellor's caseload — active plans ordered by review date (`counsellor-support-reviews-due`) — is a list opened away from any one student, and a plan has an accountable owner (`owner_id`, a `Staff` reference).
SupportPlan.crossEntity: None. Activating or closing a plan writes nothing else: in particular it does not set `Student.has_support_plan`, which is a hand-maintained flag.
SupportPlan.openQuestions: `Student.has_support_plan` and this entity say two things about one fact. The flag's own help still reads "the plan itself is held outside this system", which `SupportPlan` now contradicts, and no hook keeps the two in step. Either the flag should be derived from active plans, or its help should point here. Teachers read the plan (`adjustments`) without being able to create or change it, which is the intent of the entity's help text: the adjustments they need, without broad access to sensitive evidence.

SafeguardingConcern.placement: Standalone, and deliberately not a kind of `DisciplineIncident`: the student may be at risk rather than at fault, so the record, its readers and its lifecycle differ. The principal works a list of concerns awaiting triage (`principal-untriaged-safeguarding`).
SafeguardingConcern.crossEntity: None. A concern moving to `referred` has an `external_reference` to hold the outside agency's number, but nothing notifies that agency or anyone else; no hook or saga reads it. Closing it requires `closed_on` and a `closure_reason` — the two rules that stop a concern disappearing.
SafeguardingConcern.openQuestions: Read access is `principal` and `counsellor` only, yet `teacher` may **create**: a teacher can report a concern and then cannot see it, or its outcome. That asymmetry is intended — reporting must be easy and reading must be narrow — but the model does not say how a reporting teacher learns that action was taken, and it is the question a safeguarding lead is likely to ask first.

CommunicationLog.placement: Standalone. Failed messages across all families (`registrar-failed-communications`) are a list in their own right. Both `student_id` and `guardian_id` are optional, because a notice can concern a student without addressing one guardian, or the reverse.
CommunicationLog.crossEntity: None. The entity is the record of a message, not the sender of one: nothing in the model writes a row. `notifyGuardiansOfStatusChange` on `Student` is the only notifier the model declares, and its handler is where a row would naturally be created, but the model does not say that it is.
CommunicationLog.openQuestions: By design it stores the subject and the outcome, not the message content. Whether a guardian-facing portal may show a guardian their own log depends on row-level scoping that `%%rbac` cannot express; the `guardian` role can read this entity as a role, not as a filter.

Refund.placement: Standalone. The finance control queue — requests awaiting a decision, with age and amount (`finance-refunds-awaiting-decision`) — spans every payment, and a refund's identity is its own request, not the payment's.
Refund.crossEntity: None. A refund never edits or deletes the original payment (the entity's help says so), and no saga reads it: paying a refund does not move the invoice, which is the gap `Payment` records as an open question.
Refund.openQuestions: The entity's help says it is requested and approved by different staff "where possible", but no rule compares `requested_by_id` with `approved_by_id`. What does separate them is the role split: `finance_officer` creates, only `principal` may `approve`, and `finance_officer` pays. The master role is outside that split. Whether a refund above some amount needs a second approver is not modelled.
